items.title: Semiconductor index closes down 7.88% as renewed selling reaches Wednesday's Tokyo session
items.summary: The US semiconductor index gave back part of Monday's sharp rally, with renewed selling extending into early Wednesday trading in Japan. Analysts also lowered AI infrastructure spending forecasts, citing possible data-center delays. These are signs of continued valuation and execution risk, not proof of realized project cancellations.

observations.label: US regular-session changes, independently corroborated
observations.value: SOX Nov 20 -10.73%, Nov 23 +14.03%, Nov 24 -7.88%; Nov 24 closing level approximately 8,832.5, sources differ slightly in level.

observations.label: Tokyo November 25 early session (November 24 evening EST)
observations.value: WSJ reports Nikkei -2.8% at 57,008.52 and Advantest -12%; intraday, not confirmed closing figures. Fisco separately reports weak opening.

observations.label: Analyst forecast, not realized cancellations
observations.value: IBD reports Mizuho 2027 and 2028 AI capex projections reduced to $1.4T and $1.8T, respectively, citing potential delays/cancellations affecting 5 GW.

observations.label: Fundamental significance and next indicators
observations.value: Watch actual construction milestones, power interconnection, financing, chip orders and earnings revisions; continued strong deployments would weaken the slowdown thesis.

items.key_finding: Renewed international chip selling and lower analyst capex projections underscore infrastructure execution risk despite strong reported AI orders.

sources.title: Investor's Business Daily AI capex forecast reporting

items.title: Workday falls after hours as subscription-growth guidance tempers earnings beat
items.summary: Workday's earnings beat and growing AI contract value were overshadowed by softer near-term subscription guidance. Shares fell sharply in extended trading. Cash generation and profitability remain strong, but slowing contracted revenue growth warrants monitoring.

observations.label: Extended-hours price observation Nov 24 at 6:30 PM EST
observations.value: WiseView reports $164.50, -8.22% versus regular-session reference of $179.23; Investing.com reported -7.9% at 5:58 PM. Indicative extended-hours prices, not confirmed closing data.

observations.label: Official earnings disclosure
observations.value: Q3 total revenue $2.705B +11.2%, subscription revenue +12.8%, free cash flow $691M vs $550M, non-GAAP operating margin 31.4%; total subscription backlog +6.1%.

observations.label: Forward guidance
observations.value: Q4 subscription revenue approximately $2.6B, +10%, versus 12.8% growth in Q3; near-term forecast slightly below analyst consensus.

observations.label: Risk and next indicators
observations.value: Customer renewals, AI contract conversion, subscription backlog, margins and next regular-session price; reacceleration in subscription growth would weaken the slowdown concern.

items.key_finding: A substantial extended-hours decline contrasts with strong cash generation, but softer subscription guidance is a real fundamental risk.

sources.title: WiseView November 24 6:30 PM ET market snapshot

items.title: Separate vessel-tracking sources indicate severe Hormuz traffic restrictions
items.summary: MarineTraffic figures reported on November 24 indicate a substantial decline in weekly vessel crossings. A separate AIS tracker also shows depressed commercial transits. The data support transportation disruption but do not quantify incremental crude export losses; vessels without AIS and differing coverage limit comparison.

observations.label: MarineTraffic counts reported Nov 24
observations.value: 226 vessels Nov 1–7 versus 125 Nov 17–23, a 44.7% decline; reported by UOL.

observations.label: Separate AIS tracking snapshot Nov 24, 11:51 AM EST
observations.value: hormuz.now reports 7.4 commercial crossings/day over seven days and 2 in the prior 24 hours; differing coverage prevents direct comparison with MarineTraffic.

observations.label: Physical oil-flow assessment
observations.value: Restricted vessel movement is corroborated; incremental crude cargo volume loss and Strait-wide closure are not established.

observations.label: Next indicators
observations.value: Tanker loadings, alternative pipeline volumes, insurance, EIA Nov 25, OPEC+ Nov 29; sustained traffic recovery would weaken the disruption signal.

items.key_finding: Independent tracking indicates severe transportation disruption, but vessel counts cannot be translated directly into barrels of lost supply.

items.title: Micron falls as future memory oversupply concerns contrast with current hardware cost pressure
items.summary: BNP Paribas downgraded Micron on potential memory oversupply and data-center deployment delays. HP's evening earnings disclosure shows current memory and storage costs pressuring margins. These are distinct time horizons, underscoring the risk that capacity growth and future demand may diverge.

observations.label: Micron regular-session close Nov 24, independently matched
observations.value: $629.79, -11.01%; Yahoo Finance and Investing.com historical prices agree.

observations.label: BNP Paribas analyst forecast
observations.value: Target reduced from $1,700 to $775; possible DRAM/NAND supply-demand parity by mid-2027, not company guidance.

observations.label: HP earnings and after-hours observation
observations.value: Quarterly revenue $16.0B, +9.3% YoY; memory/storage costs pressure margins; HPQ $27.85, -0.32% after hours at 6:01 PM EST, indicative.

observations.label: Next indicators
observations.value: DRAM/NAND prices, capacity commitments, inventory, hyperscaler construction and power connections, and Micron earnings; sustained supply constraints and stronger deployment would challenge oversupply forecast.

items.key_finding: Near-term memory scarcity can coexist with medium-term oversupply risk if production and AI deployment schedules diverge.

sources.title: WSJ HP memory cost and margin report

items.title: BridgeBio advances commercialization with first FDA-approved limb-girdle muscular dystrophy treatment
items.summary: FDA granted traditional approval to BridgeBio's Welgemda on November 23, supported by Phase 3 clinical results. BridgeBio anticipates an immediate U.S. launch. Shares rose in Tuesday trading, although reported closing prices disagree. Commercial impact depends on patient identification, coverage and adoption.

observations.label: FDA approval
observations.value: Nov 23, 2026; ribitol (Welgemda) for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9; first approved therapy for a form of LGMD.

observations.label: Nov 24 market reaction
observations.value: Reported approximately +7–9%; IBD reports $85.87 and StockQuote $85.03; exact close not confirmed.

observations.label: Clinical and commercial context
observations.value: Traditional approval supported by FORTIFY Phase 3; company anticipates immediate U.S. launch and received priority review voucher.

observations.label: Next indicators
observations.value: Launch uptake, payer coverage, patient identification, durability data and additional 2027 regulatory decisions.

items.key_finding: FDA-confirmed approval materially broadens BridgeBio's commercial portfolio; revenue ramp remains uncertain.
